claim: A prior study (Tarasov et al., 2022) discovered that numerous adaptive mechanisms emerge in response to cardiac-specific overexpression of adenylyl cyclase type 8 (TGAC8) which included overexpression of a large number of proteins.
source: Our prior study (Tarasov et al., 2022) discovered that numerous adaptive mechanisms emerge in response to cardiac-specific overexpression of adenylyl cyclase type 8 (TGAC8) which included overexpression of a large number of proteins.
evidence: The claim cites a prior study (Tarasov et al., 2022) as the source of this finding.

claim: The study conducted an unbiased phosphoproteomics analysis to determine the role of altered protein phosphorylation in the adaptive heart performance and protection profile of adult TGAC8 left ventricle (LV) at 3–4 months of age.
source: Here, we conducted an unbiased phosphoproteomics analysis in order to determine the role of altered protein phosphorylation in the adaptive heart performance and protection profile of adult TGAC8 left ventricle (LV) at 3–4 months of age, and integrated the phosphoproteome with transcriptome and proteome.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental approach taken in this study.

claim: Numerous stress-response pathways within reprogrammed TGAC8 LV, including PKA, PI3K, and AMPK signaling pathways, were enriched based on differentially regulated phosphoproteins by genotype.
source: Based on differentially regulated phosphoproteins by genotype, numerous stress-response pathways within reprogrammed TGAC8 LV, including PKA, PI3K, and AMPK signaling pathways, predicted upstream regulators (e.g. PDPK1, PAK1, and PTK2B), and downstream functions (e.g. cell viability, protein quality control), and metabolism were enriched.
evidence: The claim is supported by the analysis of differentially regulated phosphoproteins in the study.

claim: Predicted upstream regulators including PDPK1, PAK1, and PTK2B were enriched in TGAC8 LV.
source: Based on differentially regulated phosphoproteins by genotype, numerous stress-response pathways within reprogrammed TGAC8 LV, including PKA, PI3K, and AMPK signaling pathways, predicted upstream regulators (e.g. PDPK1, PAK1, and PTK2B), and downstream functions (e.g. cell viability, protein quality control), and metabolism were enriched.
evidence: The claim is based on computational prediction from the phosphoproteomics data.

claim: Downstream functions including cell viability, protein quality control, and metabolism were enriched in TGAC8 LV.
source: Based on differentially regulated phosphoproteins by genotype, numerous stress-response pathways within reprogrammed TGAC8 LV, including PKA, PI3K, and AMPK signaling pathways, predicted upstream regulators (e.g. PDPK1, PAK1, and PTK2B), and downstream functions (e.g. cell viability, protein quality control), and metabolism were enriched.
evidence: The claim is supported by functional enrichment analysis of the phosphoproteomics data.

claim: Numerous kinases and phosphatases in addition to PKA were hyper-phosphorylated in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: In addition to PKA, numerous other kinases and phosphatases were hyper-phosphorylated in TGAC8 vs. WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by the phosphoproteomics data showing increased phosphorylation of multiple kinases and phosphatases.

claim: Hyper-phosphorylated transcriptional factors in TGAC8 were associated with increased mRNA transcription, immune responses, and metabolic pathways.
source: Hyper-phosphorylated transcriptional factors in TGAC8 were associated with increased mRNA transcription, immune responses, and metabolic pathways.
evidence: The claim is based on the integration of phosphoproteomics data with transcriptomics and functional pathway analysis.

claim: Many stress-response signaling pathways, i.e., PI3K/AKT, ERK/MAPK, and ubiquitin labeling, were consistently enriched and activated in the TGAC8 LV at transcriptional, translational, and PTM levels.
source: Many stress-response signaling pathways, i.e., PI3K/AKT, ERK/MAPK, and ubiquitin labeling, were consistently enriched and activated in the TGAC8 LV at transcriptional, translational, and PTM levels.
evidence: The claim is supported by integrated analysis of transcriptomics, proteomics, and phosphoproteomics data.

claim: Reprogramming of the cardiac phosphoproteome, proteome, and transcriptome confers resilience to chronic adenylyl cyclase-driven stress.
source: Thus, reprogramming of the cardiac phosphoproteome, proteome, and transcriptome confers resilience to chronic adenylyl cyclase-driven stress.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the integrated multi-omics analysis.

claim: TGAC8 markedly increases the heart rate and ejection fraction, similar to acute exercise but chronic and in the absence of corporal exertion, which persists on a 24 hr per day and 7 days per week basis.
source: TGAC8 markedly increases the heart rate and ejection fraction, similar to acute exercise but chronic and in the absence of corporal exertion, which persists on a 24 hr per day and 7 days per week basis (Lipskaia et al., 2000; Georget et al., 2002; Esposito et al., 2008; Moen et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: Despite constant high-level of heart performance driven by markedly elevated level of AC8-cAMP-PKA-Ca2+ signaling, the TGAC8 survives for an extended period of time, up to about one year of age without excessive mortality.
source: Despite this constant high-level of heart performance driven by markedly elevated level of AC8-cAMP-PKA-Ca2+ signaling, which typically proceeds to near-term cardiac dysfunction, the TGAC8 survives for an extended period of time, up to about one year of age without excessive mortality (Tarasov, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Tarasov, 2022).

claim: Adaptive mechanisms that emerge in the TGAC8 heart confer resilience to marked chronic stress of increased AC8-cAMP-PKA-Ca2+ signaling and include the enrichment and activation of a large number of proteins involved in multiple signaling pathways related to nutrient sensing, energy production, growth factor signaling, and cell proliferation.
source: Adaptive mechanisms that emerge in the TGAC8 heart confer resilience to this marked chronic stress of increased AC8-cAMP-PKA-Ca2+ signaling and include the enrichment and activation of a large number of proteins involved in multiple signaling pathways related to nutrient sensing, energy production, growth factor signaling, and cell proliferation (Tarasov, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Tarasov, 2022).

claim: Phosphorylation is one of the most important and has been the most extensively studied PTM of proteins.
source: Phosphorylation is one of the most important and has been the most extensively studied PTM of proteins.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about protein phosphorylation.

claim: Various kinases and phosphatases within cells phosphorylate and dephosphorylate, respectively, a myriad of proteins to regulate their activities and affect multiple signaling pathways.
source: Various kinases and phosphatases within cells phosphorylate and dephosphorylate, respectively, a myriad of proteins to regulate their activities and affect multiple signaling pathways.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about kinases and phosphatases.

claim: The PKA signaling pathway was highly enriched in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: Because the PKA signaling pathway was highly enriched in TGAC8 vs. WT (Tarasov, 2022), we reasoned that protein phosphorylation differed between TGAC8 and WT, and protein phosphorylation modification plays a crucial role in the remarkable adaptative capacity of the TGAC8 heart in response to markedly increased AC8-cAMP-PKA-Ca2+ signaling.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Tarasov, 2022).

claim: Protein phosphorylation modification plays a crucial role in the remarkable adaptative capacity of the TGAC8 heart in response to markedly increased AC8-cAMP-PKA-Ca2+ signaling.
source: Because the PKA signaling pathway was highly enriched in TGAC8 vs. WT (Tarasov, 2022), we reasoned that protein phosphorylation differed between TGAC8 and WT, and protein phosphorylation modification plays a crucial role in the remarkable adaptative capacity of the TGAC8 heart in response to markedly increased AC8-cAMP-PKA-Ca2+ signaling.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on prior findings and reasoning.

claim: The study identified 12963 phosphopeptides and 3646 phosphoproteins using TMT-labeling mass spectrometry.
source: By the utilization of TMT-labeling mass spectrometry (MS), we identified 12963 phosphopeptides and 3646 phosphoproteins, and observed a general upregulation of phosphorylation.
evidence: The claim is supported by the mass spectrometry data generated in this study.

claim: A general upregulation of phosphorylation was observed in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: By the utilization of TMT-labeling mass spectrometry (MS), we identified 12963 phosphopeptides and 3646 phosphoproteins, and observed a general upregulation of phosphorylation.
evidence: The claim is supported by the mass spectrometry data showing increased phosphorylation levels.

claim: The TGAC8 mouse was generated by inserting a cDNA coding for human AC8 after the murine α-myosin heavy chain promoter.
source: The TGAC8 mouse, generated by inserting a cDNA coding for human AC8 after the murine α-myosin heavy chain promoter, was a gift from Nicole Defer/Jacques Hanoune, Unite de Recherches, INSERM U-99, Hôpital Henri Mondor, F-94010 Créteil, France.
evidence: The claim describes the method used to generate the TGAC8 mouse model.

claim: Three-month-old male TGAC mice were used as study cases, and age-matched WT littermates, in the C57/BL6 background, were used as controls.
source: The 3-month-old male TGAC mice were used as study cases, and age-matched WT littermates, in the C57/BL6 background, were used as controls.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The TMT-labeling quantitative MS identified 12963 phospho-peptides and 3646 phosphoproteins.
source: The TMT-labeling quantitative MS identified 12963 phospho-peptides (File 1: Sheet 1) and 3646 phosphoproteins (File 1: Sheet 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the mass spectrometry data generated in this study.

claim: The principal component analysis (PCA) of the 3646 phosphoproteins in each mouse showed that the TG and WT samples were distinguished into two groups completely.
source: The principal component analysis (PCA) (Figure 1A) of the 3646 phosphoproteins in each mouse showed that the TG and WT samples were distinguished into two groups completely.
evidence: The claim is supported by the PCA analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Within the cutoff at -log10(p-value)>1.3 and absolute value of log2(fold-change(TG/WT))≥0.04, 781 phosphoproteins were differentially regulated by genotype.
source: Within the cutoff at -log10(p-value)>1.3 and absolute value of log2(fold-change(TG/WT))≥0.04, 781 phosphoproteins were differentially regulated by genotype.
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of the phosphoproteomics data.

claim: Of the 781 phosphoproteins, the phosphorylation levels of 741 proteins were increased and only 40 were decreased in TGAC8 vs. WT LV.
source: Of the 781 phosphoproteins, the phosphorylation levels of 741 proteins were increased and only 40 were decreased in TGAC8 vs. WT LV (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the volcano plot shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cardiac hypertrophy signaling (enhanced) is most highly activated (z-score as high as 4.867) in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: Of these pathways, cardiac hypertrophy signaling (enhanced) is most highly activated (z-score as high as 4.867) (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by the canonical pathway analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The phosphorylation status of numerous molecules, e.g., Ca2+ ATPase, RyR2, Ncx, involved in excitation, calcium cycling, contraction, relaxation, and protein synthesis, was elevated in the TGAC8 vs. WT LV.
source: The combination of (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and File 2: Sheet 2 and our recently published work (Tarasov, 2022) showed that the phosphorylation status of numerous molecules, e.g., Ca2+ ATPase, RyR2, Ncx, involved in excitation, calcium cycling, contraction, relaxation, and protein synthesis, was elevated in the TGAC8 vs. WT LV.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from Figure 1—figure supplement 1, File 2: Sheet 2, and a prior study (Tarasov, 2022).

claim: At 3-month of age, the LV mass is not elevated in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: However, we have demonstrated that at 3-month of age, the mouse age in the present study, the LV mass is not elevated in TGAC8 vs. WT (Tarasov, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Tarasov, 2022).

claim: Pathologic hypertrophic markers were not increased in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: Of note, transcriptomic, proteomic, and WB analyses indicated that pathologic hypertrophic markers were not increased in TGAC8 vs. WT (Tarasov, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Tarasov, 2022).

claim: Activated PKA signaling can restrict the activity of AC8, acting as a feedback to fine-tune the downstream signaling networks inside the body.
source: For example, activated PKA signaling can restrict the activity of AC8, acting as a feedback to fine-tune the downstream signaling networks inside the body (Willoughby et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Willoughby et al., 2012).

claim: Increased phosphorylation status of HSP90 and Akt in TGAC8 synergistically increase eNOS activity.
source: Increased phosphorylation status of HSP90 and Akt in TGAC8 synergistically increase eNOS activity (Takahashi and Mendelsohn, 2003), and increased NO produced by eNOS may modulate the function of the ryanodine receptor Ca2+ release channel (RyR2) on the cardiac sarcoplasmic reticulum (Lim et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior studies (Takahashi and Mendelsohn, 2003; Lim et al., 2008).

claim: Increased NO produced by eNOS may modulate the function of the ryanodine receptor Ca2+ release channel (RyR2) on the cardiac sarcoplasmic reticulum.
source: Increased phosphorylation status of HSP90 and Akt in TGAC8 synergistically increase eNOS activity (Takahashi and Mendelsohn, 2003), and increased NO produced by eNOS may modulate the function of the ryanodine receptor Ca2+ release channel (RyR2) on the cardiac sarcoplasmic reticulum (Lim et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Lim et al., 2008).

claim: The TMT-labeling MS identified significantly upregulated phosphorylation in the peptides of RyR2 (RISQTSQVSIDAAHGYSPR, E9Q401 [2805–2823]).
source: The TMT-labeling MS identified significantly upregulated phosphorylation in the peptides of RyR2 (RISQTSQVSIDAAHGYSPR, E9Q401 [2805–2823]) (File 1: Sheet 1), consistent with the PKA-induced phosphorylation of RyR2-S2809 mediating the increase in Ca2+ spark amplitude (Meissner, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by the mass spectrometry data and a citation to a prior study (Meissner, 2010).

claim: PKA-induced phosphorylation of RyR2-S2809 mediates the increase in Ca2+ spark amplitude.
source: The TMT-labeling MS identified significantly upregulated phosphorylation in the peptides of RyR2 (RISQTSQVSIDAAHGYSPR, E9Q401 [2805–2823]) (File 1: Sheet 1), consistent with the PKA-induced phosphorylation of RyR2-S2809 mediating the increase in Ca2+ spark amplitude (Meissner, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Meissner, 2010).

claim: The overexpression of AC8 activates the AC8-cAMP-PKA phosphorylation axis.
source: As known, the overexpression of AC8 activates the AC8-cAMP-PKA phosphorylation axis (Moen et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Moen et al., 2019).

claim: There were 2264 phosphosites whose names and locations are unambiguous within the 4990 upregulated phosphopeptides (p-value ≤0.05 and log2(fold-change(TG/WT))≥0) in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: There were 2264 phosphosites whose names and locations are unambiguous within the 4990 upregulated phosphopeptides (p-value ≤0.05 and log2(fold-change(TG/WT))≥0) in TGAC8 vs. WT.
evidence: The claim is supported by the phosphoproteomics data analysis.

claim: The majority of phosphosites were serines (S) and threonines (T), and a few were tyrosines (Y).
source: The majority of these phosphosites were serines (S) and threonines (T), and a few were tyrosines (Y) (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the composition analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A typical PKA and AKT substate motif, R-R-X-pS/T, was the most abundant substrate motif.
source: A typical PKA and AKT substate motif, R-R-X-pS/T, was the most abundant substrate motif, consistent with increased PKA-dependent phosphorylation (Figure 2B–D; Hunzicker-Dunn et al., 2012; Bellis et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by the sequence motif analysis shown in Figure 2B-D and citations to prior studies (Hunzicker-Dunn et al., 2012; Bellis et al., 2009).

claim: IPA predicted that 26 kinases were responsible for the phosphorylation motifs.
source: IPA predicted that 26 kinases were responsible for the above-mentioned phosphorylation motifs (File 2: Sheet 3), among which, three had previously been identified to differ by genotype in the LV transcriptome, 18 were shown to differ by genotype in the LV proteome, and 18 were identified in the present phosphoproteome.
evidence: The claim is based on computational prediction using IPA software.

claim: Within the phosphoproteome, eight kinases were predicted to be differentially activated by genotype, and the phosphorylation level of four of these (PDPK1, PAK1, PTK2B, and GSK3B) was increased in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: Within the phosphoproteome, eight kinases were predicted to be differentially activated by genotype, and the phosphorylation level of four of these (PDPK1, PAK1, PTK2B, and GSK3B) was increased in TGAC8 vs. WT.
evidence: The claim is based on computational prediction and phosphoproteomics data.

claim: In human glioblastoma cell lines, T98G and U87MG cells, the interference of human PDPK1 mRNA by siRNA decreased the phosphorylation level of human BAD protein (S112, S136, and S155) and activated cell death to suppress tumorigenesis.
source: For example, a previous study observed that in human glioblastoma cell lines, T98G and U87MG cells, the interference of human PDPK1 mRNA by siRNA decreased the phosphorylation level of human BAD protein (S112, S136, and S155) and activated cell death to suppress tumorigenesis (Desai et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Desai et al., 2011).

claim: In mouse myoblast cell line, C2C12 cells, PDPK1 protein phosphorylated the mouse ULK1 protein.
source: Another study reported that in mouse myoblast cell line, C2C12 cells, PDPK1 protein phosphorylated the mouse ULK1 protein (Li et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Li et al., 2018).

claim: Increased phosphorylation states of BAD (upregulated at S112, S136, and S155) and ULK1 (upregulated at S450, S521, and S637/638) in TGAC8 may be linked to activated PDPK1.
source: Increased phosphorylation states of BAD (upregulated at S112, S136, and S155) and ULK1 (upregulated at S450, S521, and S637/638) in TGAC8 may be linked to activated PDPK1.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the phosphoproteomics data and prior knowledge about PDPK1 substrates.

claim: The phosphorylation level of 27 proteins (including the three kinases (PDPK1, PAK1, and PTK2B) auto-phosphorylating themselves) were elevated by the three kinases to regulate cardiac stress signaling pathways, including PKA signaling, ERK/MAPK signaling, cardiac hypertrophy signaling (enhanced), and renin-angiotensin signaling.
source: Consistent with the IPA canonical pathway analysis, the phosphorylation level of 27 proteins (including the three kinases (PDPK1, PAK1, and PTK2B) auto-phosphorylating themselves) were elevated by the three kinases to regulate cardiac stress signaling pathways, including PKA signaling, ERK/MAPK signaling, cardiac hypertrophy signaling (enhanced), and renin-angiotensin signaling (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2), to cope with the cardiac stress in the TGAC8.
evidence: The claim is supported by the pathway analysis shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: PDPK1 phosphorylated GSK3B at S9.
source: For example, GSK3B is involved in multiple biological processes. PDPK1 phosphorylated GSK3B at S9 (Chen et al., 2013; Ericson et al., 2010) and PTK2B phosphorylated GSK3B at S9 and Y216 (Hartigan et al., 2001; Tsai et al., 2009) to inhibit the kinase activity of GSK3B.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior studies (Chen et al., 2013; Ericson et al., 2010).

claim: PTK2B phosphorylated GSK3B at S9 and Y216 to inhibit the kinase activity of GSK3B.
source: For example, GSK3B is involved in multiple biological processes. PDPK1 phosphorylated GSK3B at S9 (Chen et al., 2013; Ericson et al., 2010) and PTK2B phosphorylated GSK3B at S9 and Y216 (Hartigan et al., 2001; Tsai et al., 2009) to inhibit the kinase activity of GSK3B.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior studies (Hartigan et al., 2001; Tsai et al., 2009).

claim: In this phosphoproteome, GSK3B was phosphorylated at multiple sites, including S9, Y216, S219, and S545.
source: In this phosphoproteome, GSK3B was phosphorylated at multiple sites, including S9, Y216, S219, and S545, and thus GSK3B inhibition was linked to the cardiac adaptation (Juhaszova et al., 2004; Juhaszova et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by the phosphoproteomics data.

claim: GSK3B inhibition was linked to the cardiac adaptation.
source: In this phosphoproteome, GSK3B was phosphorylated at multiple sites, including S9, Y216, S219, and S545, and thus GSK3B inhibition was linked to the cardiac adaptation (Juhaszova et al., 2004; Juhaszova et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior studies (Juhaszova et al., 2004; Juhaszova et al., 2009).

claim: The enriched functions were mainly in three categories, i.e., cell viability, protein quality control, and metabolism.
source: To study the downstream functions of these phosphoproteins, we performed molecular and cellular functions analysis in IPA. The enriched functions were mainly in three categories, i.e., cell viability, protein quality control, and metabolism (Figure 1F and File 2: Sheet 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by the functional analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The functions of cellular assembly and organization, cellular function and maintenance, and cell death and survival were ranked as the top three terms.
source: The functions of cellular assembly and organization, cellular function and maintenance, and cell death and survival were ranked as the top three terms, indicating the important role of the reprogrammed phosphoproteome in improving cell viability in response to the chronic stress of the overexpression of AC8 in the mouse heart.
evidence: The claim is supported by the functional enrichment analysis.

claim: A moderate level of correlation of genotypic differences of molecular changes within phosphoproteome and transcriptome was observed.
source: In addition, the correlation scatter plots (Figure 3B) demonstrated a moderate level of correlation of genotypic differences of molecular changes within phosphoproteome and transcriptome, and a somewhat stronger correlation between genotypic differences of molecular changes within phosphoproteome and proteome (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A somewhat stronger correlation between genotypic differences of molecular changes within phosphoproteome and proteome was observed.
source: In addition, the correlation scatter plots (Figure 3B) demonstrated a moderate level of correlation of genotypic differences of molecular changes within phosphoproteome and transcriptome, and a somewhat stronger correlation between genotypic differences of molecular changes within phosphoproteome and proteome (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The protein phosphorylation status of about one-half of kinases, phosphatases, and TFs differed significantly (p-value <0.05) by genotype.
source: We identified 196 kinases, 71 phosphatases, and 191 TFs in the present phosphoproteome (Figure 3F). The protein phosphorylation status of about one-half of these molecules differed significantly (p-value <0.05) by genotype (Figure 3G), and the protein phosphorylation status of majority of these molecules was increased (Figure 3H–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The protein phosphorylation status of majority of kinases, phosphatases, and TFs was increased in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: We identified 196 kinases, 71 phosphatases, and 191 TFs in the present phosphoproteome (Figure 3F). The protein phosphorylation status of about one-half of these molecules differed significantly (p-value <0.05) by genotype (Figure 3G), and the protein phosphorylation status of majority of these molecules was increased (Figure 3H–J).
evidence: The claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 3H-J.

claim: Numerous phosphorylation and dephosphorylation-related biological processes and molecular functions significantly differed by genotype in the remodeled LV transcriptome of TGAC8.
source: Analysis of the remodeled LV transcriptome of TGAC8 in GO analysis using DAVID online software discovered that enrichments of numerous phosphorylation and dephosphorylation-related biological processes and molecular functions significantly differed by genotype (Figure 4A), and that the coordinated expression of numerous kinases and phosphatases also differed by genotype (Figure 4B–C and File 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by the GO analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 60 kinases were predicted to be upstream regulators of the remodeled LV transcriptome of TGAC8, and the majority of these kinases were predicted to be activated in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: Intriguingly, 60 kinases were predicted to be upstream regulators of the remodeled LV transcriptome of TGAC8, and the majority of these kinases were predicted to be activated in TGAC8 vs. WT (Figure 4D and File 9).
evidence: The claim is based on computational prediction using IPA software, shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Much fewer phosphatases were predicted between TGAC8 and WT, and most of these were predicted to be inhibited.
source: In contrast, much fewer phosphatases were predicted between TGAC8 and WT, and most of these were predicted to be inhibited (Figure 4E and File 9).
evidence: The claim is based on computational prediction using IPA software, shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Of the 191 TFs also identified in this phosphoproteome, 92 TFs differed significantly by genotype in phosphorylation status (p-value <0.05).
source: Of the 191 TFs also identified in this phosphoproteome, 92 TFs differed significantly by genotype in phosphorylation status (p-value <0.05).
evidence: The claim is supported by the phosphoproteomics data analysis.

claim: Nearly all of the TFs that differed by genotype had increased phosphorylation levels.
source: In agreement with the general upregulated transcription in TGAC8 LV (Tarasov, 2022), nearly all of the TFs that differed by genotype had increased phosphorylation levels (Figure 4G and File 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 4G and a citation to a prior study (Tarasov, 2022).

claim: The only exception was purine-rich element binding protein G (Purg), known to be hyper-phosphorylated in solid tumors.
source: The only exception was purine-rich element binding protein G (Purg), known to be hyper-phosphorylated in solid tumors (Zanivan et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Zanivan et al., 2008).

claim: Numerous immunity-related pathways, cancer-related pathways, and metabolism-related pathways were enriched in TGAC8 based on KEGG pathway analysis of hyper-phosphorylated TFs.
source: We conducted Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis to further probe the predicted facts of TFs that were generally hyper-phosphorylated in TGAC8 vs. WT. Numerous immunity-related pathways, cancer-related pathways, and metabolism-related pathways were enriched (Figure 4H and File 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by the KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 4H.

claim: The sumoylation pathway was markedly inhibited in TGAC8.
source: Intriguingly, the sumoylation pathway was markedly inhibited.
evidence: The claim is supported by the pathway analysis.

claim: The upregulated protein phosphorylation and inhibited protein sumoylation pathway in TFs coordinately activate transcription and improve immunity in the TGAC8 LV.
source: Because both sumoylation and phosphorylation are important PTMs in transcriptional regulation (Tomanov et al., 2018; Khan et al., 2014), it is possible that the upregulated protein phosphorylation and inhibited protein sumoylation pathway in TFs coordinately activate transcription and improve immunity in the TGAC8 LV.
evidence: The claim is a hypothesis based on the data and citations to prior studies (Tomanov et al., 2018; Khan et al., 2014).

claim: Numerous biological processes and molecular functions that were related to phosphorylation and dephosphorylation were enriched in the remodeled TGAC8 LV proteome.
source: Numerous biological processes and molecular functions that were related to phosphorylation and dephosphorylation were enriched in the remodeled TGAC8 LV proteome (Figure 5A), as were numerous kinases and phosphatases (Figure 5B–C and File 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by the GO analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Twenty-nine kinases that differed by genotype were predicted to be upstream regulators of the proteome, and most of these were predicted to be activated in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: Twenty-nine kinases that differed by genotype were predicted to be upstream regulators of the proteome, and most of these were predicted to be activated in TGAC8 vs. WT.
evidence: The claim is based on computational prediction using IPA software.

claim: Of the 3927 phosphoproteins identified in mouse LV samples, 2164 were identified in both the proteome and phosphoproteome.
source: Of the 3927 phosphoproteins identified in our mouse LV samples, 2164 were identified in both the proteome and phosphoproteome, and these were focused for subsequent analyses.
evidence: The claim is supported by the data analysis.

claim: After normalization, WT and TGAC8 samples manifested clear genotypic differences in PCA analysis.
source: After normalization, WT and TGAC8 samples manifested clear genotypic differences in PCA analysis (Figure 5G), and the phosphorylation status of numerous proteins normalized to the protein expression level still differed by genotype without cutoff (Figure 5H) and with cutoff (-log(p-value)>1.3 and absolute(log2(TG/WT))≥0.4) (Figure 5I).
evidence: The claim is supported by the PCA analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Even after normalizing the phosphorylation level to the protein expression level, the enrichments of canonical pathways in TGAC8 were quite consistent with those of unnormalized phosphoproteome.
source: Even after normalizing the phosphorylation level to the protein expression level, the enrichments of canonical pathways in TGAC8 were quite consistent with those of unnormalized phosphoproteome (Figure 5J and File 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by the pathway comparison shown in Figure 5J.

claim: Three signaling pathways in the TGAC8 LV, PI3K/AKT, ERK/MAPK, and ubiquitin labeling, were regulated concordantly in transcription, translation, and PTM (phosphorylation).
source: By integrating and comparing the enrichments from transcriptome, proteome, and phosphoproteome, we were able to identify the three signaling pathways in the TGAC8 LV, PI3K/AKT, ERK/MAPK, and ubiquitin labeling, that was regulated concordantly in transcription, translation, and PTM (phosphorylation) (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the integrated analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: WB validated the activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in TGAC8.
source: WB validated the activation of the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in TGAC8, reproducing the results of our prior study using different antibodies (Figure 6C–D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A (more significant)).
evidence: The claim is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 6C-D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: ERK/MAPK signaling was activated in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: We also demonstrated in that study that ERK/MAPK signaling was also activated in TGAC8 vs. WT (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B-C.

claim: Activation of PI3K/AKT and ERK/MAPK signaling is crucial for enhanced protein quality control (the increase in protein synthesis and degradation) in the TGAC8 LV.
source: Activation of PI3K/AKT and ERK/MAPK signaling is crucial for enhanced protein quality control (the increase in protein synthesis and degradation) in the TGAC8 LV (Tarasov, 2022; Figure 6—source data 1D- G).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a prior study (Tarasov, 2022) and data shown in Figure 6—source data 1D-G.

claim: WB analysis indicated that ubiquitination is increased in TGAC8 vs. WT.
source: Although protein ubiquitination, an important process in protein degradation, was enriched in TGAC8 LV within IPA analysis, its activity could not be predicted on the basis of the present knowledge base of IPA. Its WB analysis, however, indicated that ubiquitination is indeed increased in TGAC8 vs. WT (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the Western blot data shown in Figure 6E.
